subject: quant
stem: Two portfolios deliver identical cash flows on every date and have the same risk. Their market prices differ and trading is frictionless. What does no-arbitrage reasoning imply?
options: The more expensive portfolio must have better future cash flows
Both prices can persist solely because their labels differ
Buy the cheaper portfolio and sell the dearer one

subject: quant
stem: Among feasible portfolios with the same expected return, one has a lower standard deviation than all the others. How is it classified?
options: An inefficient portfolio solely because it uses diversification
A guaranteed loss-free portfolio
A minimum-variance portfolio at that return

subject: quant
stem: A regression of a stock’s excess return on market excess return has slope greater than one. Under the CAPM interpretation, what does that slope estimate?
options: The stock’s total standard deviation
Above-market systematic risk exposure
A guaranteed positive abnormal return

subject: econ
stem: A government borrows to raise spending when resources are already heavily utilized. Which concern is most directly associated with the borrowing?
options: A necessary fall in private borrowing costs
Guaranteed repayment without future fiscal consequences
Possible crowding out through pressure on interest rates

subject: econ
stem: Government spending rises, but taxes rise by even more. Why is the spending change alone insufficient to identify the overall fiscal stance?
options: Any increase in spending is always expansionary overall
The net effects of spending, taxes and cyclical conditions must be considered
Tax changes have no effect on aggregate demand

subject: ci
stem: A corporate shareholder sells all her shares to another investor. Which consequence is generally most accurate?
options: The corporation must liquidate when an owner exits
All company debts become the seller’s personal debts
The corporation continues despite the ownership transfer

subject: ci
stem: A private company considers a public listing. Which trade-off is most relevant?
options: Guaranteed cheaper funding with no new obligations
Broader access to investors with greater disclosure and compliance obligations
Permanent exemption from market scrutiny

subject: ci
stem: A company has a high current ratio, but most current assets are slow-moving inventories. Which assessment is most appropriate?
options: Near-term payment capacity also depends on asset quality and cash timing
A high current ratio guarantees that every bill can be paid on time
Inventories must be valued at zero for all liquidity analysis

subject: ci
stem: A treasurer reduces inventory without disrupting operations and collects receivables sooner. What is the most direct working-capital benefit?
options: A necessary increase in financing needs
Less cash tied up in operating assets
A guaranteed increase in product selling prices

subject: ci
stem: A project evaluation includes money spent last year that cannot be recovered. How should that amount enter an incremental cash-flow analysis?
options: Include it solely because it was large
Treat it as an opportunity cost of an alternative use today
Exclude it as a sunk cost

subject: ci
stem: An issuer balances interest tax benefits against expected financial-distress costs when choosing leverage. Which view is reflected?
options: The trade-off approach to capital structure
A rule that all firms should finance entirely with debt
A claim that operating risk is irrelevant to leverage

subject: fsa
stem: Under IFRS, development costs of an internally generated intangible asset are:
options: Always expensed as incurred, together with research costs
Always capitalized, whether or not any criteria are met
Capitalized once specified criteria are met, with research costs expensed

subject: fsa
stem: A company reports rising net income, but its operating cash flow is negative because receivables and inventory have grown far faster than sales. What is the most reasonable interpretation?
options: Profit is not turning into cash, so earnings quality and collectibility need checking
Strong performance, because net income is rising and the business looks healthy
Nothing unusual, because operating cash flow is always volatile from year to year

subject: fsa
stem: A company's note on share-based compensation shows that the number of stock options outstanding has risen sharply and many are in the money. What is the most relevant implication for existing shareholders?
options: None, because options are excluded from the financial statements
A reduction in the company's reported long-term debt
Exercise would dilute their ownership, and the options carry a compensation cost

subject: fsa
stem: A company uses straight-line depreciation for its financial statements and accelerated depreciation for tax. How should the resulting difference be classified?
options: A temporary difference, because it reverses over the life of the asset
A permanent difference, because it is never reversed
No difference, because both methods use the same cost

subject: fsa
stem: A regulator reviews only a small share of company filings each year. What does this imply about regulation as a disciplining mechanism?
options: It deters through the chance of review, but limited capacity means much low-quality reporting can go unchecked
It guarantees that all misreporting is found within a year
It has no deterrent effect, since most filings are never reviewed

subject: fsa
stem: A company reports "adjusted earnings" that exclude restructuring charges, which have occurred every year for five years. What should an analyst conclude?
options: The charges appear recurring, so the adjusted figure may overstate sustainable earnings
The adjusted figure is more reliable than net income
The exclusion is always required by the accounting standards

subject: fsa
stem: An analyst wants to compare an industry-specific measure across several companies. What is the main risk?
options: Industry-specific measures are always identical across firms
Companies may define the measure differently, so figures need to be checked for consistency
Such measures can be compared only within a single company

subject: fsa
stem: An analyst uses last year's margin to forecast earnings for a company that has just made a large acquisition. What is the main weakness?
options: Margins can never be used for forecasting
The company's cost structure and business mix have changed, so past margins may no longer apply
Acquisitions never affect margins

subject: fsa
stem: A company with a strong competitive position in its industry is most likely to be able to:
options: Charge lower prices than every rival while raising margins
Avoid all changes in input costs
Pass cost increases on to customers and protect its margins

subject: fsa
stem: In an inflationary period, a company with strong pricing power is most likely to see its operating margin:
options: Largely preserved, because it can raise prices as its costs rise
Fall sharply, since costs always rise faster than prices
Rise automatically without any price changes

subject: eq
stem: A company issues two equity classes with identical dividend rights but unequal votes per share. What can differ between their owners?
options: Their dividend entitlement solely because votes differ
The legal identity of the corporation
Influence over corporate decisions

subject: eq
stem: A benchmark includes only firms from one industry, rather than the entire domestic market. How is it best classified?
options: A broad-market index solely because it contains several firms
A sector equity index
A fixed-income maturity index

subject: eq
stem: A company completes a stock split without changing its assets or liabilities. What is the immediate mechanical effect for an owner?
options: More shares with a proportionately adjusted price per share
A guaranteed increase in the total value of the holding
A cash distribution equal to the split ratio

subject: eq
stem: A buyer purchases shares on the ex-dividend date under the usual ex-dividend convention. Who ordinarily receives the upcoming dividend?
options: The buyer always receives it because settlement occurs later
Both parties receive the full distribution
The seller retains the upcoming dividend entitlement

subject: eq
stem: An analyst’s estimated intrinsic value exceeds the observed share price. What conclusion follows within that analyst’s model?
options: The market price must immediately equal the estimate
The share appears undervalued relative to the estimate
The estimate is guaranteed correct because it differs from price

subject: eq
stem: A firm’s dividends are far below sustainable distributions because it retains excess cash. Which issue should an analyst consider in selecting a valuation model?
options: Whether dividends represent the cash flow relevant to equity owners
Whether a dividend model is compulsory for every listed issuer
Whether retained cash is always worthless

subject: eq
stem: A diversified firm sells products in several industries. Why may a single industry classification be inadequate for peer selection?
options: It can obscure different business-segment exposures
Classification guarantees that all segments have identical economics
A legal corporate name determines every operating exposure

subject: eq
stem: A return model includes separate exposures to inflation surprises and changes in industrial activity. What distinguishes it from the single-factor CAPM?
options: It represents more than one systematic return driver
It assumes all risk is company-specific
It automatically eliminates model misspecification

subject: fi
stem: A speculative-grade issuer has limited unsecured borrowing access. Compared with a strong investment-grade issuer, which feature is more likely in its debt financing?
options: A guaranteed lower spread solely because credit risk is higher
Greater covenant protection and a higher required credit spread
No sensitivity to collateral or debt seniority

subject: fi
stem: An analyst compares a benchmark sovereign bond market with the market for small corporate issues in the same currency. Which contrast is commonly relevant?
options: Government and corporate debt always have identical default risk
Every sovereign bond is necessarily risk-free
Issue size, trading liquidity and credit-risk exposure

subject: fi
stem: A bond seldom trades, so an analyst estimates its price using yields on actively traded bonds with similar maturity and credit quality. What technique is this?
options: Pure historical-cost accounting
An assumption that all bonds have the same coupon
Comparable-bond matrix pricing

subject: fi
stem: A floating-rate note’s required discount margin rises above its contractual quoted margin, with other conditions unchanged. Where is its price most likely relative to par near a reset?
options: Below the note’s par value
Above par because required compensation rose
Always exactly at par regardless of the margins

subject: fi
stem: A par yield for a given maturity is determined from the spot curve. What coupon rate does it represent?
options: The spot rate at every cash-flow date simultaneously
The rate that makes the bond’s price equal par
A coupon guaranteed to remain the current market yield forever

subject: fi
stem: A fixed-rate bond investor sells before maturity. Which combination is needed to assess total holding-period return?
options: The original coupon rate alone
Coupon receipts, reinvestment income and the sale price
Only the final maturity principal that the investor never receives

subject: fi
stem: A portfolio duration is calculated as a market-value-weighted average of constituent durations. Which limitation is especially important?
options: It guarantees immunity to all changes in the yield curve
It makes credit spreads irrelevant to bond prices
It summarizes a parallel-shift exposure rather than every curve movement

subject: fi
stem: An interest-rate change can alter whether a callable bond is redeemed early. Why is effective duration useful?
options: It revalues cash flows that can change with the yield curve
It assumes all cash flows remain fixed regardless of exercise
It measures only the contractual coupon

subject: fi
stem: A borrower defaults. One debt claim is secured by collateral and another is an unsecured subordinated claim. Which statement is generally most accurate?
options: The secured claim has stronger priority against its collateral
All claims must receive identical recoveries
Subordination gives the junior claim first access to collateral

subject: fi
stem: A lender pools loans and sells securities backed by the pool to investors. What potential benefit does this provide?
options: A guarantee that the loans can never default
Access to funding through the pooled assets
Automatic elimination of all capital and legal requirements

subject: fi
stem: A securitization issues senior and junior tranches. Which internal protection most directly supports the senior tranche?
options: Equal loss absorption by every tranche at all times
Subordination of the junior tranche
A guarantee that collateral value never falls

subject: fi
stem: A fully amortizing residential mortgage has fixed scheduled payments, and payments are made as contracted. What happens to the principal balance over time?
options: It declines as principal is repaid
It remains unchanged until a single final bullet payment
It grows solely because the coupon rate is fixed

subject: fi
stem: A residential MBS passes borrowers’ cash flows to holders after servicing charges. What feature must investors still model?
options: Only the original stated maturity with certain cash-flow dates
The timing of prepayments and the resulting cash-flow changes
A permanent separation from all mortgage-credit exposure

subject: fi
stem: A commercial mortgage pool contains loans with substantial balloon balances due at maturity. Which risk deserves particular attention?
options: Refinancing risk at the balloon payment date
The assumption that all principal was already amortized
Only homeowners’ seasonal prepayment habits

subject: deriv
stem: A buyer has the right, but no obligation, to acquire an asset at a stated exercise price. What distinguishes this claim from a forward purchase?
options: Both parties must always exchange the asset at maturity
Exercise is optional for the buyer
The seller can cancel a valid exercise whenever it is unfavorable

subject: deriv
stem: A firm uses a derivative to reduce exposure to a known future foreign-currency payment. Which benefit is most directly sought?
options: Creating a guaranteed speculative profit
Eliminating all operating risks of the business
Reducing uncertainty in the domestic-currency payment

subject: deriv
stem: A futures contract is marked to market daily while an otherwise similar forward settles at maturity. What is the key economic difference?
options: The timing of realized cash flows
The underlying can never be the same
The futures buyer never faces gains or losses

subject: deriv
stem: For the same underlying and maturity, futures price changes tend to be positively correlated with interest rates. Under the usual daily-settlement argument, how can this affect the futures price relative to the forward price?
options: It necessarily makes both prices identical under all conditions
It must make the futures price lower
It can make the futures price higher

subject: deriv
stem: Why does a call option’s nonlinear payoff require a different replication argument from a simple forward payoff?
options: Its holder must always buy the underlying
Its exposure changes with the underlying price
Its payoff is always a fixed amount

subject: deriv
stem: A binomial option valuation uses risk-neutral probabilities. Which interpretation is correct?
options: They must be the investor’s actual subjective probabilities
They prove investors are literally indifferent to all risks
They are pricing weights consistent with traded-asset prices

subject: alt
stem: An investor buys a stake alongside a private fund in a particular portfolio company. Which method best describes the stake?
options: Co-investment alongside the sponsor
A purchase solely of the fund’s pooled units
A mandatory public-market index allocation

subject: alt
stem: A private fund manager earns a recurring management fee and a share of investment profits subject to agreed conditions. What best describes the second component?
options: A guaranteed fixed coupon paid by every portfolio company
An incentive or performance allocation
An investor’s committed but uncalled capital

subject: alt
stem: A database includes only hedge funds that are still operating. What performance-measurement concern is most immediate?
options: A guarantee that the sample represents failed funds
Survivorship bias
The elimination of all selection effects

subject: alt
stem: A listed real estate vehicle is compared with a directly owned building. Which distinction is most accurate?
options: Listing removes all real estate cash-flow risk
A listed claim is identical to owning a specific building outright
The listed claim can be liquid while retaining exposure to property economics

subject: alt
stem: A timberland owner can postpone harvesting during a weak lumber market while trees continue to grow. Which feature is most relevant?
options: A requirement to harvest all trees immediately at any price
The absence of fire, weather and operating risk
Flexibility in harvest timing coupled with biological growth

subject: alt
stem: An investor gains digital-asset exposure through an exchange-traded product rather than self-custody. Which issue still requires analysis?
options: The assumption that all operational risks vanish
The product’s custody, fees and tracking arrangements
The absence of any link to the underlying asset

subject: alt
stem: A portfolio’s digital-asset allocation is justified only by one short period of low correlation with stocks. What is the main weakness?
options: Low sample correlation proves permanent diversification
The estimate may be unstable across market regimes
All digital assets have identical liquidity and custody risk

subject: pm
stem: An investor chooses the point where an indifference curve is tangent to an available capital allocation line. What is being selected?
options: The most preferred feasible risk-return combination
The riskiest feasible portfolio regardless of preferences
A portfolio with a guaranteed realized return equal to its expectation

subject: pm
stem: Two risky assets have correlation below perfect positive correlation. What is generally possible by combining them?
options: A guaranteed elimination of all portfolio risk
A diversification benefit relative to their weighted average volatility
A requirement that expected return be zero

subject: pm
stem: A model decomposes a security’s return into sensitivity to common factors and a residual unique to the security. What does the residual represent?
options: A guaranteed positive alpha
The return component unexplained by the specified common factors
The risk-free rate by definition

subject: pm
stem: An adviser evaluates a new holding by its effect on the client’s entire portfolio rather than its stand-alone volatility. Which principle is being applied?
options: A requirement to ignore correlation
A rule to select each asset solely by its own past return
The portfolio approach

subject: pm
stem: A client states a return objective after inflation and fees. What should the manager do when comparing it with a forecast before inflation and fees?
options: Convert both measures to a consistent basis
Compare the numbers directly without adjustment
Treat all inflation assumptions as realized certainties

subject: pm
stem: A firm has risk models but no clear ownership, reporting escalation or limits. What framework weakness is most apparent?
options: Too much certainty about actual future losses
Insufficient governance and integration into decision-making
A requirement to abandon all quantitative analysis

subject: pm
stem: A pension sponsor has limited ability to fund a severe asset shortfall. What should this imply for its risk tolerance assessment?
options: A higher target return alone creates greater loss-bearing ability
Loss-bearing capacity should constrain risk taking
Risk tolerance must be inferred solely from recent market returns

subject: eth
stem: An adviser says a questionable sales practice is fine because "everyone in this market does it." Which criticism identifies the flaw most precisely?
options: Being common describes what people do, not whether the practice meets principles such as honesty
Common practice can never be ethical, so anything that is widely done should be avoided
The practice must be unethical because it has not been written into the firm's formal policy

subject: eth
stem: A new advisory firm prints a code of ethics and puts it on its website but never trains staff on it or discusses real cases. Which assessment is most reasonable?
options: It helps only if people understand and apply it; publishing it alone does not ensure conduct
The firm is now an ethical firm because a written code exists and is publicly available
Codes never influence conduct, so the firm has lost nothing by leaving it unexplained

subject: eth
stem: Research on ethical behavior suggests that whether a person acts ethically in a difficult moment is most influenced by which of the following?
options: The person's own internal character traits, considered on their own
Their belief that they are honest people who would never do such a thing
External situational influences, such as what the people around them are doing

subject: eth
stem: Which statement about ethical and legal standards is most accurate?
options: Laws often codify ethical expectations, but ethics can require more than the law does
Conduct that is legal is always ethical, so a lawful act needs no further ethical scrutiny
Ethical standards and legal requirements never overlap in any area of professional life

subject: eth
stem: For the purposes of Standard II(A), information is "material" when it:
options: It has already been reported in a company's regulatory filings and is available to all
It would probably affect a security's price, or a reasonable investor would want it
It comes from a source inside the company rather than from public documents

subject: eth
stem: An analyst plans to start her own advisory firm. While still employed she calls the firm's current clients to say she will soon be offering the same service and asks them to move their accounts. Which is the best assessment?
options: A violation: she may prepare to leave but must not solicit clients while employed
No violation, because she has not yet formally left the firm she works for
No violation, because clients are always free to choose whichever adviser they wish

subject: eth
stem: What is a supervisor required to do under Standard IV(C)?
options: Personally review each and every trade and communication made by the people they supervise
Take reasonable steps to catch and stop breaches of law and the Code by people they oversee
Be responsible only for violations that they personally commit and never for others

subject: eth
stem: A research note states "Company X's shares will double next year because demand is surging." The analyst has no data showing the doubling. What is the main problem under V(B)?
options: The note contains a forecast, and a forecast is never permitted in a research note
The problem exists only if the shares later fail to double as the note predicted
An opinion is presented as fact, but facts and opinions must be kept distinct

subject: eth
stem: A manager moves clients' portfolios into a strategy that relies heavily on derivatives, a material change from the process described to clients. She plans to mention it in next year's annual letter. Which is the best assessment?
options: A violation, because material changes to the investment process must be disclosed promptly
Acceptable, because the annual letter is the usual channel for telling clients things
Acceptable, because clients can always ask if they want to know about changes

subject: eth
stem: A member could easily avoid a conflict by reassigning coverage of a company to a colleague. Instead she keeps the coverage and discloses the conflict in small print. What is the best assessment?
options: Adequate, because disclosure is always an acceptable alternative to avoiding a conflict
Adequate, provided that the client signs the form containing the small-print disclosure
Not adequate: she should avoid it where reasonable, and disclosure must be prominent

subject: eth
stem: When must referral arrangements be disclosed to a client?
options: Before the client commits to the referred service, so she can judge any partiality
After the referral fee has actually been received by the adviser or the firm
Once a year, in the firm's general annual report to all clients

subject: eth
stem: An adviser learns that his firm's marketing shows returns gross of fees without saying so, and it has already gone to prospects. Which response would best conform?
options: Leave it as it is, because prospects can always ask about fees if they want to know
Label or restate the returns so fee effects are clear, and correct material already sent
Correct only the materials that are sent out from now on, and not the earlier ones

subject: eth
stem: When local securities regulations are less restrictive than the CFA Institute Code and Standards on a professional practice, Standard I(A) Knowledge of the Law requires a CFA charterholder to:
options: Follow the CFA Institute Code and Standards because they are stricter
Follow local securities regulations because statutory law always governs
Follow local regulations after obtaining written client consent

subject: eth
stem: An executing broker invites a buy-side trader to an all-expenses-paid luxury resort weekend with no business agenda, shortly before the firm's annual broker-allocation review. To comply with Standard I(B), the trader should:
options: Attend the weekend if the trader's employer has no written travel policy
Attend the weekend and allocate trades solely on execution quality
Decline the invitation because lavish hospitality could reasonably compromise objectivity

subject: eth
stem: Under Standard I(E) Competence, a CFA charterholder who begins advising clients on newly introduced structured credit products must:
options: Rely solely on the product issuer's marketing brochure for risk disclosures
Limit advice to clients who already hold a CFA charter
Acquire the necessary knowledge and skills before advising clients on those products

subject: eth
stem: A seasoned CFA charterholder has covered industrial equities for 12 years. Two years after major lease-accounting standards changes took effect, he continues valuing industrial firms using his legacy pre-change operating-lease adjustments because he has not updated his technical knowledge of the revised standard. Which statement best describes his obligation under Standard I(E) Competence?
options: He complies with I(E) because extensive sector experience establishes ongoing competence
He violates I(E) because competence requires ongoing learning as standards and regulations evolve
He avoids an I(E) issue because outdated accounting inputs fall solely under diligence, not competence
